speaker: A

text: Well, it's extremely important. And look, the President has organized a sea change for this industry. This is an industry that's been broadly beaten down, kicked down, victims of lawfare, victims of overregulation in a way that we've never seen before. You know, the attacks that were coming from inside of government stifled innovation, they stifled growth. And the President gave a direct mandate. We want to be the crypto capital of the world here in the United States. I think that we are, and we will persist as such with the direction that we're moving. You know, in the President's first Digital Assets Executive Order, he did something that was extremely important. He established the Digital Assets Working Group inside of the White House in which we were able to pull really all of the relevant agency actors, from the CFTC to SEC to treasury to Commerce to doj, any of the actors inside of government that touched anything regarding the space. And he had some important landmarks in this Executive order as well. You know, we had the 30 day landmark which required these agencies to do an internal audit or review of anything they touched regarding digital assets more generally. The 60 day landmark compelled the same actors to provide a list of recommendations, things that they could do independently to usher in change and create a innovation friendly environment here in the United States. We're now looking at this 180 day landmark in which we have a report which all of our colleagues are diligently working on, which will basically be a book that says, look, this is the clearest regulatory environment we could possibly have to usher in the golden age for digital assets here in the United States to onshore folks that have left, and ensure that the relevant actors here can have access to the capital markets of the United States in ways they've never had before. And so if you want to be the crypto capital of the world, you need companies innovating here, you need builders developing here, you need companies Ipoing here at the end of the day, and we're focused on all of those things. I think we're well on our way of delivering on the president's promises, and I'm sure we'll get into the legislative initiatives that are underway. But we've looked at this thing really in three stages. We've had the demolition phase. The president was very clear he wanted to eradicate anything that undergirded operation choke point 2.0. And I think that we're, you know, we've done a lot of that heavy lifting already. We're moving on to the construction phase in which, you know, we have the genius act that's moving full head of steam in the Senate right now on stablecoin legislation. We'll get into market structure shortly thereafter. The staffers and House Financial Services with Chairman Hill have done phenomenal work with that just in terms of revamping fit. Right. You know, giving us a good work product. That's a starting point in which we can have healthy conversation about how do we create this robust, clear environment that allows for innovation. I think we're well on our way of achieving both of these legislative priorities before August. We're moving at tech speed, as our brilliant AI and crypto czar likes to say. David Sacks. And it's really just an exciting time.

text: I'm starting to get this question quite a bit. Well, look, let's go back to the strategic bitcoin reserve and the precedent that the president set with that. He was adamant that bitcoin is digital gold and should be treated as such as the United States of America. We've done that by setting up the SBR again, leading the globe in terms of our acceptance of this asset class and what it means for the American people. We wanted to harness that and we also wanted to recognize what's happening in other ecosystems and encourage that as well, which is why we have the digital assets national stockpile. You know, look, we, we firmly understand that bitcoin is unique. It's a commodity, not a security, has intrinsic stored value, as David likes to say. It has the immaculate conception. Right. But look, inside of this executive order, there were really two big things that took place. One, we said we are no longer going to sell bitcoin as a country, period. Again, we want to harness this asset for the American people. And then two, we can look at budget neutral ways that don't cost the taxpayer a dime of accumulation. And I get asked all the time from different journalists, you know, how much do you want? I'm like, that's a very silly question for the United States of America. We want as much bitcoin as we can possibly accumulate. And so we're fleshing out these ideas with the folks over at treasury, the folks at Commerce. If you read the EO and the fine print, it kicks, you know, a lot of the responsibility in terms of producing these ideas over to these interagency actors. But we'll flesh that out amongst the working group and then we'll move on those that are most expeditiously implemented. But that's not to say it's one size fits all. I mean, there's countless ways in which we can do this. We've certainly heard several Great ideas. And as the president likes to say, he has a lot of high IQ people in his cabinet. So we'll continue to work out exactly what this is going to look like, but I can assure you that we'll move quickly on it.
